<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD contains only standard top-level variable assignments (pkgname, pkgver, pkgrel, pkgdesc, arch, url, license, depends, makedepends, source, sha256sums) and function definitions (build, check, package). Running `makepkg --printsrcinfo` sources these assignments and defines the functions, but does not invoke build(), check(), or package(). There are no command substitutions, network fetches, eval statements, or obfuscated payloads at the top level. The source array is a static string and is not downloaded during sourcing. This is consistent with ordinary packaging practice and poses no risk at this narrow gate.
</details>

LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
  <decision>SAFE</decision>
  <details>
    The PKGBUILD is a conventional AUR package definition for the xombe library. It specifies pkgname, version, architecture, source URL (the official GitHub archive), dependencies (glibc, cmake), and build steps using cmake in Release mode with shared libraries enabled. The build() function invokes cmake -S ... -B build ... followed by cmake --build build. The check() runs ctest. The package() installs the built files and copies the LICENSE file to the target prefix. All network activity is limited to downloading the source tarball from the project's own GitHub repository, matching the declared source field. No curl, wget, eval, or base64 decoding appears. The checksum is supplied but not cross-verified; however, a missing checksum alone is not a security threat. No post-install hooks modify system-wide configuration or execute arbitrary code outside the package scope.
  </details>
  <evidence/>
  <summary>PKGBUILD appears benign, standard packaging, no malicious network calls.</summary>
</security_assessment>
